items.title: Phil Schaap interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 9, 2003
items.q: And then I’d go hear Roy Eldridge... And then I said, 'Of course he’s Roy Eldridge’s piano player.'

ctx.x: That’s what I’m calling the rhythmic revolution of the thirties. There’s an innovation of genius. Roy Eldridge, Billie Holiday, Charlie Christian, Benny Carter, Benny Goodman, Teddy Wilson, Lester Young if I haven’t said him of course, and a few others. But the transference of it to others and the coherence of it as an ensemble display where the parts are combinable and examinable separately, I hear that merger in the Basie band first, other than an individual display. Billie Holiday displayed it on her lonesome,…
Right. How did you find them overall as people?
